new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (no catalog record, existing_statements empty). First evidence held by the project for Lapuyan/Southern Subanen word stress, but it is transcribed wordlist data (SIL 80204 Lapuyan 1953; SIL 80769 Lake Wood 1967; SIL 80208 Siay 1965), not an author's rule statement; it points to non-fixed, penult-dominant lexical stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No listed SIL item states a stress rule; the only prose about stress is the notational sentence quoted (stress written with an apostrophe before the stressed syllable). The evidence is per-word stress marks in the wordlists, read from the page scan: Conklin 1953 Lapuyan column (p. 4, 27 items / 28 words): penult in 23 words ('sambag, 'ma?an, ma'latan, 'dugu?, 'tʰulan, 'duru?..), final in 1 (magga'tut), first syllable in 4 longer or reduplicated forms (pa'gitubu?, 'mannangi, 'manukmanuk, 'pʰayupʰas); Brichoux & Hall 1967 Lake Wood list (pp. 2-3, items 1-59, my count of the marked forms): about 25 penult ('bunga, 'gabu, 'buta, 'dugu?, 'manok, kʌ'labʌw, hi'yupon, 'dlawas..) against about 9 final (mʌsi'pʌg, bʌlʌ'rʊt, sʰʌlʌ'man, sʊmin'sʊl, lʊbɨ'ngɨn, gɨ'dʌb, momo'nek, mʌgʌ'lʊd, gʌ'ga), several items unmarked. Reading (inferred from transcription only, hence low confidence): stress is not fixed; it is predominantly penultimate with a lexical minority of final-stressed words (and initial stress on some longer forms), i.e. the usual Philippine-type lexical penult/final contrast. The 2016 orthography guide (SIL74550, written for Central Subanen) gives spelling rules only: doubled vowels aa ii ee uu 'used only when a word is uttered longer', grave mark for glottal stop, no stress or accent rule; the 1985 and 1992 phrase books have no pronunciation notes (a full-text search for stress/accent/pronunc = 0).
new_statements.secondary_stress: none marked: one stress mark per word; two-word items carry one mark each ('gisid 'tubig), the reduplication 'manukmanuk carries a single initial mark
new_statements.exceptions: only the recorders' caveat 'In a few cases, the recorders forgot to record stress' (unmarked items are therefore not evidence of anything); dialect columns differ on some items (Miatan du'ru? final vs Lapuyan 'duru? penult, p. 4 item 23)
new_statements.identity_note: SIL 80204's fourth column is Subanun 'at Lapuyan' (Zamboanga del Sur; informant Emma Bayamban, 1953) = Lapuyan Subanun proper; SIL 80769 is Subanon of Lake Wood (Lakewood, Zamboanga del Sur, 1967) and SIL 80208 Subanon of Siay (Zamboanga del Sur/Sibugay, 1965-75), both catalogued by SIL under Southern Subanen [laa] and both showing the Southern Subanen aspirates; SIL 74550 is a Central Subanen [syb] orthography guide with Southern Subanen dictionary/story sections; the phrase books have a Southern Subanen column. The other Conklin columns (Miatan, Malayal, Lituban, Zamboanga del Norte) are Western/Northern Subanen-area varieties, not laa.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean Languages: Issues in Description, Subgrouping, and Reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 462 pp.http://hdl.handle.net/10125/101972
sources.note: Ch. 10 (Subanen subgroup; 10.3 Proto-Subanen phoneme inventory and reflexes incl. SSUB = Southern Subanen; 10.6 reconstructions) and sec. 5.8 (Southern Subanen ablaut, Table 5.25) contain no statement about Southern Subanen word stress; Subanen daughter forms are written without accent marks while PGCPH etyma carry them (e.g. *bátaʔ, *balú), but this is never commented on. Only general remark: p. 287 fn. 3 (Maranao chapter) 'most languages native to Mindanao and areas further south have lost contrastive stress'. Sec. 8.2.9 'Contrastive Accent' (p. 259) concerns Manide/Inagta Alabat only.

sources.citation: Finley, John Park & William Churchill. 1913. The Subanu: Studies of a Sub-Visayan Mountain Folk of Mindanao. Washington: Carnegie Institution of Washington (Publ. 184).https://archive.org/details/subanustudiesofs00finl
sources.note: Ch. II 'Subanu phonetics and composition members' (p. 55): vocabulary recorded without diacritics, 'the whole topic of pronunciation.. must necessarily be omitted'; no stress rule. Data are from Sibuguey-peninsula Subanu generally (Sindangan Bay, Dinas, Dumankilas), not Lapuyan specifically. Later 'accent upon the ultima' remarks (p. 116 and the talo entry) are Churchill's Polynesian comparisons, not Subanu rules.
